title: Spezzatino di Manzo
subtitle: Italian braised beef with wine, celery, and tomato
excerpt: Chunks of beef braised slowly in red wine and tomato until completely tender. Serve with polenta or crusty bread to catch the sauce.
sourceNotes: Classic Italian beef stew, common in home kitchens across Lombardy, Tuscany, and Lazio.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely before freezing. Keeps for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Brown the beef in batches so the pan stays hot and the meat colours properly.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead. The stew improves overnight as the sauce deepens. Reheat slowly before serving.

content.text: Spezzatino means cut into pieces. The beef needs long, low heat to break down the connective tissue and become tender. Brown each piece well before adding any liquid. That step builds the deep colour and flavour that carries the whole stew.
Pat the beef dry and season with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with flour and shake off any excess.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over a high heat. Brown the beef in batches until well coloured on all sides, about 3 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the red wine and let it simmer for 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the base.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the tinned tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, and bay leaves. Stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Put the lid on, slightly ajar, and cook on a low heat for 90 minutes. The beef should break apart when pressed with a spoon.
Remove the rosemary and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 90 minutes.
items.cause: The heat was too high, causing the meat to tighten rather than relax.
items.fix: Turn the heat to its lowest point, add a splash of water, replace the lid, and cook for another 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The lid was fully closed so no steam could escape.
items.fix: Remove the lid and cook on a medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes to reduce the liquid.

items.symptom: The beef did not colour properly when browning.
items.cause: Too many pieces were added to the pan at once, lowering the temperature.
items.fix: Brown in smaller batches. Each piece needs space and a hot pan to colour rather than steam.
